title: Every number carries a unit, a period and a comparison
note: A figure says what it measures, over what period and against what, so it can be judged at a glance.
intent: A bare 1,284 tells a person nothing. Every headline number gets a label (what it measures), a unit (€, ms, users), a period (last 7 days) and, where it helps, a comparison (+12% vs. previous period, with an arrow and a colour that also has text). Format numbers for people: thousands separators, sensible rounding, compact notation for large values, a dash for missing data rather than 0 or NaN. Order the cards by importance, with the figure largest and the label smallest. Never show undefined, NaN or a raw ISO timestamp.

check.ask: Does every headline number show what it measures, its unit and its period, so it can be understood without guessing?
check.note: Every figure on the dashboard has a label, a unit and a period.

port: One `stat({ label, value, unit, period, change })` component renders every figure, so no card can leave a field out.
